The obvious design is a status called `amended`, and it was rejected twice over: a note reopened to be corrected is NOT finished, so labelling it `amended` would show a half-rewritten clinical record as though it were signed; and "has this been amended, and how often" is answered by COUNTING the snapshot rows on every read, where a stored counter would be one more thing that can disagree with the rows it counts. 0067 already ENFORCED the design that follows — its CHECK says a note in draft or in_progress has no completed_at and no finalised_by, so reopening must clear both, which is right rather than merely required: a reopened note has no signature, and naming who signed the replaced version would attribute a record they have not seen. Who signed it is in the snapshot, where it stays true. THE SNAPSHOT IS A FULL COPY, NOT A DIFF: a diff of a clinical record is only readable beside the thing it applies to, and after two amendments nobody can reconstruct the middle version without replaying them in the right order. This is the ONE place in the feature that copies clinical values rather than pointing at them, because here going stale is the entire purpose. Re-finalising goes through completeConsultation UNCHANGED, so an amendment cannot be used to get around the type gate. //lastChange: Consultation phase 3 — the record's integrity (2026-09-28). §32's amendment, §39's entered-in-error refined, the per-note audit view and the permission model. 0070 adds consultation_amendments and no status value; see //counts for why a fifth status was rejected. Amending snapshots the whole note FIRST, in the same transaction, then reopens it — the order 0060 settled for diagnostic reports, because if the update succeeds and the snapshot does not then what the record said is gone, which is what §32 exists to prevent. Two entered-in-error holes were closed: a retired note can no longer be AMENDED back into the record (§39 exists to prevent exactly that laundering), and it can no longer be RE-MARKED, which used to overwrite error_reason — losing the only explanation the record has — and put a second ENTERED_IN_ERROR on the audit trail for something that happened once. Five mutations were run against the service and each turned exactly the right test red: no snapshot, snapshot taken after the reopen, and each of the three guards removed. On the client, a note nobody has corrected says NOTHING about versions (never "Original", never "Version 1", never "No amendments" — all three are claims about a history nobody has looked at), and the history shows an event type it has no wording for by its raw name rather than dropping it, because a history that silently omits what it cannot label reads as complete when it is not.
